title: NDA Review and Redline Suggestions
summary: Review incoming NDAs against your playbook, produce tracked-change redlines with comments in Word, and send only the non-standard ones for full lawyer review, so routine NDAs stop queuing.

seo.title: NDA Review and Redline Suggestions with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that reviews NDAs against your playbook, drafts tracked-change redlines in Word with comments and escalates non-standard terms to a lawyer.

problem.intro: NDAs are the agreement most legal teams see most often: before every vendor evaluation, partnership discussion or senior hire. Most are close to standard, but each still needs a careful read for an over-broad definition, a hidden non-solicit or a one-way obligation, and the queue holds up the business.

pain_points.title: Routine work, constant volume
pain_points.detail: Lawyers redline the same clauses again and again while sales and procurement wait to start conversations.

pain_points.title: Traps in short documents
pain_points.detail: Residuals clauses, non-solicitation, perpetual terms and broad injunctive relief hide in otherwise ordinary NDAs.

pain_points.title: Counterparty paper varies
pain_points.detail: Every counterparty uses its own template, structure and numbering, so a checklist alone does not help.

pain_points.title: No negotiation memory
pain_points.detail: Positions agreed with a counterparty last year are not visible to the lawyer reviewing the next NDA with them.

solution.overview: We build an NDA assistant that takes the counterparty's Word or PDF draft, identifies whether it is mutual or one-way and who the parties are, and checks each clause against your playbook: definition of confidential information, exclusions, permitted and compelled disclosure, term and survival, return or destruction, residuals, non-solicitation, remedies, governing law and jurisdiction. It produces a Word document with tracked changes and margin comments explaining each edit in your house style. NDAs within playbook fallbacks are marked standard for a quick lawyer sign-off; anything outside goes to a lawyer with the issues listed. Past positions agreed with the same counterparty are shown alongside.
capabilities: Identifies NDA type, parties, purpose and governing law from any template
Clause-by-clause comparison with your standard and fallback positions
Tracked-change redlines and margin comments in native Word format
Detects residuals, non-solicitation, perpetual terms and other non-standard provisions
Shows positions previously agreed with the same counterparty
Triage into standard, edits within fallback, or escalate to a lawyer

workflow.title: Receive the draft
workflow.detail: The business submits the counterparty NDA through an intake form or a shared mailbox.

workflow.title: Identify structure
workflow.detail: Parties, type, purpose and clause structure are identified whatever the template.

workflow.title: Check against the playbook
workflow.detail: Each clause is compared with your positions and fallbacks, and missing protections are noted.

workflow.title: Draft redlines
workflow.detail: Tracked changes and explanatory comments are generated in the counterparty's own document.

workflow.title: Triage and review
workflow.detail: Standard NDAs go to a lawyer for quick sign-off; non-standard ones go with an issue list.

workflow.title: Send and record
workflow.detail: The approved redline goes to the counterparty, and final positions are saved for next time.

inputs: Counterparty NDA drafts in Word or PDF
Your NDA playbook with standard and fallback positions
Previously negotiated NDAs with the same counterparty
Request details: purpose, business owner and urgency
outputs: Word document with tracked changes and comments
Record of agreed positions per counterparty
Turnaround and volume reports for legal operations
human_in_the_loop: A lawyer signs off every NDA before it is sent, including those marked standard. Non-standard provisions and anything outside the playbook are decided by a lawyer, who can edit or discard any suggested redline.
guardrails: Redlines use only approved clause language from your library
Every suggested change carries a comment giving the playbook reason
No NDA sent without lawyer sign-off
Counterparty drafts processed in your environment and not used for training
Playbook changes versioned and approved by the legal team
compliance_notes: Supports review by your lawyers; it does not provide legal advice.
NDA records include personal data of signatories; designed to support DPDP Act 2023 safeguards.

pilot.scope: Inbound NDAs from one business unit, with every redline reviewed by a lawyer and compared with what they would have drafted.
deliverables: NDA playbook encoded with your legal team
Comparison report of suggested and final redlines

what_we_measure.how: Suggested changes kept, edited or removed by the reviewing lawyer.
Non-standard provisions found by lawyers but not flagged.
Time from intake to redline sent, compared with recent NDAs.
How often the lawyer agreed with the standard or escalate classification.

faqs.q: Will the redlines look like our own?
faqs.a: Yes. Edits come from your approved clause library and comments follow your house style, so the counterparty sees your usual positions.

faqs.q: Can it handle NDAs in different formats?
faqs.a: Yes. It identifies clauses by meaning rather than numbering, so it works across counterparty templates, converted PDFs and mutual or one-way structures.

faqs.q: Do lawyers still need to read every NDA?
faqs.a: Yes, but standard NDAs arrive with the redline and checks done, so sign-off is quick. Non-standard ones arrive with a clear issue list.

faqs.q: How long does it take to set up?
faqs.a: A typical pilot runs for three weeks, most of it spent encoding your playbook and testing on recent NDAs. Production timing depends on your CLM and intake tools.
